[b]Albic Coal, Shamatine Ore | [sub]Commonwealth Palace, Kingsmount | 23 February 2024 [/sub][/b]

It was a warm day at Kingsmount. This was now the second meeting of a committee of trade representatives and business executives on the topic of High Albany's resurgent mining sector. The second, having followed from an initial meeting about two days ago on developments in the White Sea. Now, they had convened to discuss the matter of [url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=rmb/postid=58571879]Elladi's recent proposal[/url], which has started a buzz among Albic business circles. The smell of freshly brewed coffee lingered as Minister of Foreign Affairs, Alice Ostman, prepared her opening statement.

"The Commonwealth trade representative has forwarded to us the intents of the Republic of Elladi on the sale of bauxite and bituminous coal. Domestic confidence in the foreign markets are at an all-time high, so we have to act quickly. Mr. O'Reilly, Ms. Loder, and Mr. Almstedt, you've been selected as representatives of High Albany's corporate interests. I'm sure you've combed over the Elladikoan proposal already."

[list]

"Yes Ms. Ostman, we have." Mr. O'Reilly of ACG responded. "ACG Industries resolved our views in a meeting last week, though our position hasn't changed. Coal exports are a crucial sector for many Albic states, and certainly CD$90 makes sense at the moment. However, coal futures have always been volatile, especially thanks to green party interference. If the price dips to CD$80, CD$75, we'll be stucking paying for above-market rates until 2035. We can't justify that."

"And it's the same with bauxite." Ms. Loder of Cordis nodded in agreement. "CD$289 is a price that a hobbyist will go after, but not us. The EEC presented the bid on their own terms. They're lowballing it because the know they'll be able to take the loss until market values naturally start to appreciate."

[/list]

"Bold claim, Ms. Loder." Ostman responded, furrowing her eyebrows. "But I can understand it. We're now in an unprecedent period of international militarization. That said, I'm sure that the EEC actually proposed the fixed rates to sweeten the deal, not leave some landmines for us to step on. If there's a global chain disruption, a fixed rate allows us to hedge against potential uncertainties. It's the same with coal. Mr. Almstedt, you have your hand raised, go ahead."

[list]

"Thank you AJO." Xavier Almstedt remarked casually as he shifted in his seat."

"Decorum, Mr. Almstedt." Ostman retorted, nonplussed at the mention of her non-standard nickname.

"Sorry, sorry, Ms. Ostman... Ahem, so ladies and gentlemen, I hear your concerns, but let's be rational for a second." Xavier continued as he folded his arms. "Personally, I like the fixed rates, but I can understand how they might trap us later down the line. Though at the same time, I can't imagine accepting a fully adjustable rate either. We cannot put our mining sector through ten years of enforced speculation, and especially not now while the futures of metals and coal are both completely volatile at the moment."

[/list]

The table murmured for a few seconds. Ms. Loder seemed to raise her hand to question where Xavier was going with his statement, though the latter would cut through the morass of discussions, continuing with a stern voice.

[list]

"Fixed rates can work. No, they will work, but we need safeguards." He reasoned. "My suggestion is this: Consult with the Kingsmount Metals Exchange and the Stormhaven Index for the benchmark indices, then negotiate a hybrid model. If base rate for bauxite is CD$289 per ton, let's negotiate adjustments with the EEC every two years if market flunctuations exceed 15% in either direction."

"The same could be negotiated with coal." Mr. Gardell of CIO Group, a major Almstedt subsidiary, would affirm as he expanded on his superior's proposal. "We can have CD$90 be the base and index it on global trends, though with a floor of CD$85 to prevent sellers from crashing."

"Adjustments without the volatility." Xavier nodded. "What do you guys think?"

[/list]

The business executives on the committee exchange whispers to one another as they discussed Almstedt's proposal, while Minister Ostman steepled her fingers together, quietly assessing the room's mood. So far, it seems that Almstedt's proposal showed promise.

[list]

"ACG Industries will be willing to move forward with the deal if a hybrid model like this is adopted, Ms. Ostman."

"Same with Cordis." Ms. Loder followed up.

[/list]

Minister Ostman would visibly be seen breathing a sigh of relief. She briefly turned to Xavier, who would wink in her general direction. Scowling, she combed over her notes again to affirm Almstedt's model. In essence, the EEC's proposed fixed rates would be honored, but with the inclusion of biennial adjustments to account for global flunctuations exceeding 15%, along with a floor of CD$85 for Albic coal exports. While it was obvious from this that the Elladikoans will also try to negotiate their own floor for bauxite imports, for now the committee was unanimous. Might as well present these terms first and let the Elladikoans try and better it for themselves afterward.

[list]

"Alright." Ostman would say as she turned the page of her personal notebook. "Next is logistics. Mr. Almstedt, you said before that you were willing to shoulder the initial burden for expanding High Albany's present port infrastructure?"

"Yes Ms. Ostman." Xavier quickly responded. "We currently have prospects of expanding three deep-water ports, two at Kingsmount and one at Stormhaven. That'll require no less than CD$500 million, of which Dearborn Bank has pledged to answer 25%."

"ACG Industries also wishes to negotiate favorable contracts for our heavy equipment to optimize any expansions to High Albany's mining operations."

[/list]

"That can be done." Ostman swiftly responds as she finalizes their discussions in a small note. "Alright, to reiterate... we'll be requesting Commonwealth bauxite imports at a base rate of CD$289 per ton, with biennial adjustments if global prices shift by over 15%. Commonwealth coal exports at a base rate of CD$90 per ton with a floor of CD$85, with biennial adjustments if global prices shift by over 15%. There will be no new or import/export restrictions with Elladi for 10 years. On the domestic side, the Commonwealth shall award a $500 million contract in port infrastructure to Almstedt Corporation and Dearborn Bank, together with preferential contracts for ACG Industries and other Commonwealth heavy equipment suppliers. We might also require the creation of an Albo-Elladikoan oversight committee to streamline compliance and renegotiation. Is that all good and clear?"

[list]

"Yes." The whole commitee responded in unison.

"Alright. I'll submit our findings to the Chambers and see what they think, though I have confidence that our representatives will understand what is best for our country. If things go well, we'll have an MOU by the middle of March and ratification soon after."

[/list]

As the meeting adjourns and the business executives exchange handshakes, Xavier turned to Ostman and murmured something inaudible. Ostman's mouth cracks briefly into a subtle smirk before dissipating back into a cool, flat countenance as the two departed to prepare the report.

Later that day, a finalized version of High Albany's position on Elladi's trade proposal would be submitted, outlining their request for price floors and adjustable rates.

[quote=oppressive_airstrikes;58571879][b][u]Elladikoan Armed Forces conduct "Dysei-2" exercise[/u][/b]

It would seem as though the province of Kavala would not return to a relative state of peace, as the revelry of citizen crowds during the election was replaced by a decidedly different source of noise. Just in time as the State of Elladi announced that the 2nd Combat Group of The National Defense Forces would be conducting a military exercise, were tanks already rolling across the grasslands, shrubs and abandoned fields that lay in fallow. They were accompanied by a hundred or so more lighter machines, carrying weapon specialist teams and infantry squads, camoflagued in a gentle, brown pattern similar to the red soil of the region. Great trails of crushed soil drew a picture of a mobile force conducting long-spanning sweeps, mock raids and coordinated flanking exercises. A great deal of mockup targets were surrounded, by-passed or simply obliterated by this initial sweeping ground wave.

Above them, in an otherwise sunny and clear blue sky, several dozen helicopters joined this wave of war machinery, exercising their capabilities in acting both as close air support or a decidedly mobile means to get supplies or soldiers into the fray in areas otherwise unreachable by tracked or wheeled means. Complimenting this lighter air force were elements of the 2nd Combat Group's own fleet of multirole aircraft, which seemed to be exercising their own form of raiding: deep strikes, on small or almost invisible targets behind the designated "enemy line".

If there is anything that the exercise has shown to be true, it is the fact that Elladi is capitalizing on abandoning the old Chalkassean Authority's far more scripted, levy-intense doctrine for a more modern means of waging warfare, focused on leader initiative, mobile logistics and increased focus on precision bombing and targetting of important enemy military or logistical infrastructure.

The exercise has, however, highlighted the need for Elladi to further expand it's own electronics industry and the related light industrial sector. The external systems of NDF tanks and fighting vehicles were reportedly not always able to recognize targets, nor were dive-bombs always accurately released on targets. The provincial press and the nation's state outlet has repeated what the NDF office has said to the exercise, declaring it as a success in "adjusting our citizen army to a new means of warfare."

The Elladi Unity Party (EUP) has highlighted the need for increased defense spending to compliment any industrial expasion, come the end of the military exercise and the release of the official results.

[b][u]No coal? No, charcoal![/u][/b]

Western Shamat was not always a region devoid of coal, but it certainly become one given the needs of the former Chalkassean empire's need for industrial expansion. The scars are still visible here and there: Swiftly depleted open pit mines in the provinces of Patreia, Halcionida and Katereia, they were swiftly reclaimed by nature like one would put a bandage over a cut for it to heal. Not that nature had any means to regrow, for the environment of the highlands and mountains was still put for use to carry on industrializing Elladi, limited as that project was during the century of steam in the Chalkassean Authority.

The Authority made use of a relatively capable, large-scale charcoal production industry to fuel the smelteries, refineries and blast furnaces of the imperial entity. It is a system inherited by the republic, although modern times have permitted for a more sustainable production of charcoal, as crude oil has been partially redirected by the state to phase out coal as a primary means of combustion and power generation.

Yet as useful as this inherited and slightly unburdened charcoal production complex may be, the forest coverage within Elladi has been steadily declining over the time this system has been put into place. The nation's state outlet has announced that the republic would set in motion a project that'd bring about a more energy-intense, reliable form of coal input through foreign trade, so as to phase out and cool several locations' charcoal ovens, for the benefit of the nation's environmental beauty, biodiversity and overall health.

[b][u]New Prospects[/u][/b]

The Elladikoan Economic Council, being the representative of the Republic of Elladi's national economic framework, has begun drafting the paperwork necessary to formalize a potential trade agreement with several prospective foreign nationstates. Prior, detailed information was already present concerning the foreigners, as the Armed Forces' own staff was regularly in contact with the EEC given it's importance as a planning bureau.

The first two drafts have already been developed into actual propositions.

[b]1. Official Communique of The Republic of Elladi for The Republic of [nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation][/b]
[i]- In accordance with The Elladikoan Armed Forces Special Interest Directive[/i]

The Republic of Elladi invites the foreign party to consider the proposition of beneficial trade, presented as such:

[spoiler]
[list=1]1) For the Republic of Elladi to offer the ULR access to Provincial Bauxite & Aluminium markets.[/list]
[list=2]2) For the ULR to offer the Republic of Elladi access to ULR Lumber & Related markets.[/list]
[list=3]3) The Republic of Elladi is not opposed to further re-negotiation of presented terms at the behest of the addressed party.[/list]
[/spoiler]

[b]2. Official Communique of The Republic of Elladi for The Commonwealth of [nation]High Albany[/nation][/b]
[i]- In accordance with The Elladikoan Armed Forces Special Interest Directive[/i]

The Republic of Elladi invites the foreign party to consider the proposition of beneficial trade, presented as such:

[spoiler]
[list=1]1) For the Republic of Elladi to offer the Commonwealth of High Albany a fixed trade agreement concerning the export of Elladi State and Provincial Bauxite & Aluminium resources into the Commonwealth of High Albany.[/list]
[list=3]1.1) Beginning at the EEC calculated, generous bid of 289 USD$ (or whatever the Cordone equivalent is) per ton of Bauxite Ore. [/list]
[list=2]2) For the Commonwealth of High Albany to offer the Republic of Elladi a fixed trade agreement concerning the export of medium-grade coal into the Republic of Elladi.[/list]
[list=3]2.1) Beginning at the EEC calculated bid of 90 USD$ (or whatever the Cordone equivalent is) per ton of Bituminous Coal. [/list]
[list=4]3) The Republic of Elladi is not opposed to further re-negotiation of presented terms at the behest of the addressed party.[/list]
[/spoiler][/quote]

The request of access to Lavian lumber markets is granted for such access offered in the deal, although due to the current unrest in Elladi, the National guard will be monitoring and guarding the border and connecting roads and railways between the Swabati provinces and Elladi .
